messages:
devon: Heads up — after re-ingesting the curation bank embeddings with qred-4b-quant we ran the normal dedupe pass and saw ~12% fewer duplicates than the fp baseline. Suspect fingerprint/hash change.
priya: Ugh. Do you have a minimal diff sample we can inspect?
devon: Yep, pulled two sample docs. Notice fp changed even though text identical.
```
# doc_id: 0xA12
old_fp: 0x7f3a9b2e (xxhash64)
new_fp: 0x1c4e5d99 (siphash64)
# doc_id: 0xB77
old_fp: 0x8a9c3d44
new_fp: 0x8a9c3d44  # stayed same in this case
```
jonas: We rolled a transitive dependency bump on the fingerprinting crate yesterday (xxhash -> siphash by default) as part of the quant build container. That would explain consistent shifts.
alice: If the dedupe signal changed, label queues will diverge — some items we expected to collapse will show as unique. We just started a reassign yesterday so this could add noise. Can we translate new_fp -> old_fp to maintain continuity for running label batches?
marco: From an eval standpoint this is noisy but manageable if we mark the affected runs. The bigger problem is if the dedupe delta preferentially drops short prompts or code prompts — that would bias our quality stats. Quick check: can we get a stratified diff by length & token type?
devon: +1 on stratified diff. I ran a quick split: duplicates lost are mostly short conversational snippets and some system prompts. Not great.
label-bot: dedupe-pipeline: job 429 paused (manual) — awaiting handoff.
jonas: Short-term options: 1) rollback the fingerprinting lib in the quant ingest pipeline (fast), 2) add a compatibility translator that recomputes legacy fp from the new embeddings (medium), 3) re-run full dedupe with new fps and rebaseline downstream labels (slow).
alice: Rollback feels safest for ongoing labeling. Translator is nice for audit & replay. We need a path that avoids reassigning >3k in-flight tasks.
sarah: Customer-facing question — any chance this changes model selection in the canary? i.e., if dedupe drops different prompts, our evals could tilt and cause the wrong rollout decision.
devon: Good point — if we don't stabilize, comparisons between qred-4b-quant and qred-4b-fp-safe will be noisy. Proposing immediate rollback for the ingest pipeline + parallel work on translator.
priya: I'll own the translator proto (small script: map new_fp -> regenerate old_fp using legacy tokenization + xxhash64). Can post PR by EOD.
jonas: I'll kick the rollback and pin the container to previous hash; will also snapshot the digests. Rollback complete: 1734511200 :white_check_mark:.
marco: Once translator PR is up, can you run a 10k sample and push stratified diff to the eval dashboard? I can compare metrics.
devon: Action items: (1) jonas rollback (done), (2) priya proto translator PR, (3) alice check labeler queues & pause reassigns until we have translator results, (4) marco run stratified eval, (5) devon will run a quick backfill with legacy fps on a 50k slice.
alice: Paused reassigns and will flag any urgent reviewer tasks.
priya: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/qred/compat-fp — includes script and small test vectors.
label-bot: dedupe-pipeline: job 429 resumed (manual) — translator job queued.
devon: Thanks all. Triage note: avoid merging any ingestion changes that touch fingerprint crate until we have compatibility tests in CI. :thinking:
marco: I'll annotate the canary evals to ignore runs between 1734508000-1734512000 until we confirm stability.
sarah: Good catch; please add a short blurb in release notes so CS knows why a small batch of customer prompts may have different de-dup footprints.
devon: Will do. Follow-ups: update on translator results + label impact by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
